guarded_evaluation.description: modes 2 and 3 disabled; mode 1 requires a predicted gain above 1500 cash
guarded_evaluation.interpretation: The safety gate correctly fell back to V022c everywhere, so it added no measurable upside.

findings: Mode 1 is highly opponent-dependent: the large positive and negative deltas came from random, while starter, V022c, and V18 were usually exact no-ops in the tested windows.
Against the newer high-score opponents, mode 1 was an exact no-op in all 32 tested late-window interventions.
Modes 2 and 3 have only tiny late-window effects and negative or near-zero means; they should not be enabled by default.
The merged ridge model selected mode 1 at every decision boundary, showing that sparse cash-delta data produced a global action bias rather than a robust contextual policy.
The apparent gain is below the 0.5 percent promotion threshold and the sample is too small for an online submission.
decision: Keep V022c as the control and retain RL-002 only as an experiment. Do not replace main.py or generate a promoted RL submission.
next_research: Record whether an overlay actually changes the submitted market list before fitting a model.
Train an effective-action gate first, then fit the cash delta only on effective interventions.
Use deterministic opponents and several independent seeds for calibration; treat random-opponent results separately.
Model product-level price and order collision outcomes instead of fitting final cash directly.
